title: Probe-design-sprint-manifest-and-metric-experiment-canvas
content:
Purpose and context:

This doc is a lightweight sprint manifest + experiment canvas for designing, shipping, and validating small observability probes tied to feature rollouts. It focuses on three practical outcomes:
1) a small set of precise metric definitions required to evaluate a rollout hypothesis,
2) a minimal tracing annotation plan to support end-to-end investigation, and
3) a dashboard tiling and alert scaffold that keeps query cost bounded.

Why this exists:
- Our rollout cadence needs a repeatable pattern to add instrumentation without exploding signal surface area.
- Shipping too many adhoc metrics leads to technical debt and high query cost.
- Teams need a simple canvas to capture the hypothesis -> probe -> acceptance loop.

When to use it:
- Small to medium feature rollouts (canary -> global) where behavior and cost must be monitored.
- Quick experiments where we need deterministic pass/fail criteria for quality/cost tradeoffs.

Sprint Manifest (1-2 week probe sprint):
- Kick (Day 0): owner sync with product/eng/exec on hypothesis and success criteria.
- Day 1: finalize metric & trace plan on this canvas. Keep to <= 6 metrics.
- Day 2-4: instrument and land lightweight metrics + traces. Prefer adding tags/attributes to existing spans rather than new span types.
- Day 5: smoke validation with synthetic traffic and local dashboard.
- Day 6-7: deploy canary with sampling and watch grouped panels.
- Post-sprint: decide (promote, iterate, rollback). Archive experiment details.

Experiment Canvas (fill during Day 1):
- Hypothesis (one sentence): e.g. "Routing heuristic X will reduce p99 latency by >= 25% for multi-part requests without increasing token cost > 3%."
- Feature owner: string
- Probe owner (observability): string
- Critical follow-ups: short list

Metric selection guidance (hard guardrails):
- Max 6 metrics for primary canvas (1 primary SLI, 2 quality indicators, 1 cost indicator, 1 availability indicator, 1 warm-start/KV indicator).
- Metric names MUST follow metric-naming-style: obs.<service>.<area>.<measure> (e.g., obs.inference.kv_cache.hit_rate).
- Do not create per-tenant metrics unless the signal will be used in a chargeback or quota decision. Use tags instead.
- Prefer ratios and quantiles (p50/p90/p99) over averages for latency.

Suggested metric definitions (copy/adapt):
- obs.inference.latency.request_p99_ms -> Description: end-to-end request latency, p99.
  - Unit: milliseconds
  - Source: service edge histogram (sum/count buckets)
  - Alert threshold (canary): increase > 30% vs baseline over 10m

- obs.inference.success_rate -> Description: fraction of requests with 200-level generation responses (no fallback).
  - Unit: ratio
  - Calculation: successful_requests / total_requests
  - Alert: drop below 99.5% for >5m on canary

- obs.inference.kv_cache.hit_rate -> Description: fraction of token cache hits for warm-starts
  - Unit: ratio
  - Source: runtime KV metrics tagged by model and tenant
  - Use: correlated with cost and latency regressions

- obs.inference.token_cost_per_1k -> Description: estimated token cost normalized per 1k tokens
  - Unit: dollars per 1k tokens (or internal cost-units)
  - Calculation: cost_aggregation / tokens_processed * 1000

- obs.inference.model-fallback.count -> Description: count of fallbacks to cheaper/older model variants
  - Unit: count
  - Use: guardrail for graceful degradation policies

- obs.inference.session-cold-start-rate -> Description: fraction of sessions requiring full KV rehydrate
  - Unit: ratio
  - Use: track rollout effects on cache warmth and upstream backend load

Tracing & annotation plan (minimalist):
- Trace goals: 1) ability to follow a single request across routing -> model -> kv-cache -> tokenizer; 2) find where p99 mass accumulates.
- Sampling: enable full tracing for canary cohort (100% for canary sessions), 0.5% for baseline traffic.
- Required span attributes (attach to existing spans, do not add new top-level spans unless necessary):
  - trace.attr.feature_flag = <feature_name_or_variant>
  - trace.attr.route_decision = <routing_policy_id>
  - trace.attr.model_variant = <model_semver_or_tag>
  - trace.attr.kv_hit = true|false
  - trace.attr.token_count = integer
  - trace.attr.tenant_id = <tenant_id_or_anonymized>
- Key trace anchors: client->edge (ingress), router->model_worker (dispatch), model_worker->kv (cache), model_worker->executor (generation). Keep spans coarse-grained; avoid per-token spans.

Dashboards: tiling, query cost, and alert scaffold
- Tiling pattern (per rollout):
  - Row 1 (health): request rate, success_rate, error_rate (5m)
  - Row 2 (latency): p50/p90/p99 heatmap + small histogram snapshot
  - Row 3 (cost): token_cost_per_1k, kv_cache.hit_rate, model_fallback.count
  - Row 4 (traces): sampled trace waterfall count and top 5 root-cause tags
- Query budget guardrails: each panel must document estimated query cost (low/med/high). Prefer pre-aggregated metrics or rollups with 1m resolution. Use sampling for histograms where possible.
- Dashboard naming: obs-rollout.<feature>.<canary|global>.<date>
- Small operator checklist (first 30 minutes): check health row, then latency row, then cost row. If any critical thresholds hit, flip circuit-breaker to fallback variant.

Alerting & Severity mapping (canary phase):
- Sev1 (automated rollback): sustained success_rate drop > 2% absolute for 10 minutes AND p99 latency increase > 40% vs baseline.
- Sev2 (investigate): token_cost_per_1k increase > 10% for 15m OR kv_cache.hit_rate drop > 20% relative.
- Sev3 (informational): small anomalies or debug-only signals.

Acceptance criteria (for promoting a rollout):
- Primary SLI (e.g., p99 latency) meets target relative to baseline for 1h under production traffic.
- Cost uplift < allowed delta (as specified in the feature PR).
- No increase in model_fallback.count beyond baseline tolerance.
- Traces captured for 95% of canary sessions (sampling policy met).

Investigation templates (when things go wrong):
- Step 1: correlation panel: show p99 latency vs kv_cache.hit_rate and request rate.
- Step 2: open top 5 sampled traces tagged with route_decision to see where time concentrates.
- Step 3: check recent deployments + config changes (linked PRs).
- Step 4: if fallback count increased, inspect routing policy rollout matrix and model variant metrics.

Implementation notes / quick wins:
- Add attributes to existing spans rather than creating parallel telemetry pipelines. This reduces storage and preserves correlation.
- Implement a small synthetic probe that runs a 3-turn conversation to exercise KV, tokenization, and generation; run at 1qps for canary namespaces.
- Use precomputed rollups for p99 over 1m windows to avoid expensive raw histogram queries.

Open questions & risk register (to resolve during sprint planning):
- Tenant privacy: do we need to hash tenant_id in traces for regulated customers? (owner: Security)
- Cost attribution accuracy: token cost approximations are noisy; do we need to route billing telemetry to Finance for authoritative numbers? (owner: Finance/Platform)
- Rollback latency: what is expected cost of automated rollback (resource churn, cache cold-start)? Need simulation.

Action items (for next sprint):
- [ ] Fill experiment canvas for current feature PR (owner: feature lead).
- [ ] Implement the 6 metrics listed and tag spans with required attributes (owner: telemetry engineer).
- [ ] Create rollout dashboard template and assign operator checklist (owner: observability PM).
- [ ] Run synthetic probe in staging and measure query cost (owner: SRE).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the canvas terse; teams get overwhelmed by too many signals. If a metric is not actionable within 15 minutes, drop it from primary canvas.
- Archive the experiment in Confluence with links to PRs and dashboard snapshots for future audits.

Appendix: useful query snippets (examples)
- p99 latency (example-ish): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- kv hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hit_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_request_total[5m]))
- fallback count: sum(increase(model_fallback_total[10m]))

End of manifest.

If you want, I can convert this into a template Google Doc with fields pre-filled for the next rollout and a checklist that integrates with JIRA.
